messages:
maya: Heads-up — small but consistent NDCG/MRR drop on the new reranker variant (v3.1-ptq) when queries hit short docs (<64 tokens). Quick numbers below, noticed in canary evals.
cheng: ah ok, can you paste the numbers?
maya: ```
model            | ndcg@10 | mrr@10
-----------------|---------|--------
float32 v3.1     | 0.321   | 0.402
ptq int8 v3.1    | 0.297   | 0.374
delta            | -7.2%   | -6.9%
slice: short-docs (<64 tokens)
```

nate: that's not tiny. Any tokenizer or preprocessing changes between runs? often short-doc regressions are tokenization/clipping related.

maya: No tokenizer model changes in this rollout. The only change was an optimization in the quantization pipeline — we switched to a new "kvpack-first" merge that touches sequence packing before tokenization-normalization. Repro artifacts: run://evals/2026-03-18/ptq-shortdoc.json

sara: @maya can you diff token counts/boundaries between the float32 and ptq runs? if BPE splits shift, ranking can flip for short docs.

maya: quick diff done — mismatch in ~3.2% of docs. Mostly docs ending with punctuation or trailing whitespace. Example: "Error reading config..." tokenized to ["Error"," reading"," config","..."] vs float32 ["Error"," reading"," config..."] — so boundary shift.

cheng: hmm that's interesting. Could the packing change be merging suffix tokens differently, causing different input to the model for PTQ path?

nate: also check candidate ordering is identical in evaluation harness — we had a bug last quarter where negative sampling ordering changed between preprocess steps.

maya: harness ordering is identical. Also dumped raw scores for a few sample queries. Example dump:
```
query: "how to rotate disk"
candidates:
 - docA tokens=48 score_float=2.15 score_ptq=1.98
 - docB tokens=12 score_float=1.74 score_ptq=1.86
(note: ptq promotes shorter docB for some queries)
```

sara: that pattern (short doc promotion) matches the token-boundary hypothesis. If PTQ alters the tokenization or sequence padding, logits can shift earlier.

nate: my hunch: int8 kernels + kvpack-first reorder the input chunks so attention context alignment is slightly different; for long docs it averages out, for short docs it tips ranking.

maya: plan: 1) run ptq variant with kvpack disabled (ptq-no-kvpack), 2) run ptq but with an explicit post-normalization step to align token boundaries (ptq-norm), 3) collect per-query token mismatch stats and slice-level NDCG/MRR. Will queue both jobs.

sara: :thumbsup: also add a small AB: float32 vs ptq-no-kvpack on the same sample. If ptq-no-kvpack matches float32, rollback pack change in PTQ pipeline.

eval-bot: Scheduled eval jobs 5641 (ptq-no-kvpack) and 5642 (ptq-norm). ETA ~45m. Links: https://evals.redwood/jobs/5641, https://evals.redwood/jobs/5642

maya: thanks, I'll post results here. If regressions persist after both, we'll pin back to float32 for canary and open a rollback PR for the PTQ packing change.

cheng: also please add a corpus sample of the failing docs so we can write a targeted unit test for tokenization parity. we shouldn't rely on manual diffs long-term.

maya: will add 500-sample holdout and open the test. tagging @nate for kernel/kvpack investigation.

nate: on it. I'll reproduce a microbenchmark for attention alignment with int8 kernels.

maya: thanks all. updating thread when jobs finish. :hourglass:
